# llms.txt template (v2)

`llms.txt` is a **community proposal** by Jeremy Howard / Answer.AI, first
published in 2024 and revised to v2 in 2026. It is **not** a W3C/IETF standard
and **not** a confirmed ranking factor. No AI system guarantees it reads the
file. Publishing one does not improve rankings by itself.

Use it to give agents a concise, curated map of your best content.

---

## 1. Minimal valid file

```markdown
# Example Ltd

> UK ecommerce engineering studio building Shopify and Magento platforms.

Example Ltd designs, builds, and supports commerce platforms for UK retailers.
We publish technical guides, migration checklists, and platform comparisons.

## Services

- [Technical SEO](https://www.example.com/services/technical-seo.md): audits, fixes, and monitoring for commerce sites.
- [Platform migration](https://www.example.com/services/migration.md): replatforming without traffic loss.
- [Shopify development](https://www.example.com/services/shopify.md): theme, app, and checkout work.

## Guides

- [SEO migration checklist](https://www.example.com/guides/seo-migration-checklist.md): URL mapping, redirects, and launch monitoring.
- [Core Web Vitals for ecommerce](https://www.example.com/guides/core-web-vitals-ecommerce.md): LCP, INP, and CLS fixes by template.

## Company

- [About](https://www.example.com/about.md)
- [Contact](https://www.example.com/contact.md)

## Optional

- [Case studies](https://www.example.com/case-studies.md)
- [Careers](https://www.example.com/careers.md)
```

## 2. Format rules (v2)

- File name: `llms.txt`, at the site root or any subpath.
- Markdown, UTF-8, optional BOM.
- **Required:** exactly one H1 with the site/project name.
- **Recommended:** a blockquote summary immediately after the H1.
- Optional prose sections. Only H2 headings are used to group file lists.
- H2 sections contain markdown lists of links:
  `- [Title](https://example.com/page.md): optional note`
- `## Optional` is conventional for secondary links agents can skip.
- Links should be canonical, live, and useful.
- Keep it small enough to fit in a context window; detail lives behind links.
- Do not dump the entire site, keyword lists, or marketing fluff.
- Keep it current; stale links erode trust.

## 3. Markdown mirrors

v2 recommends clean markdown versions of pages:

- `page.html.md` (append `.md`) or `page.md` (replace extension).
- Directory URLs: `index.html.md` or `index.md`.
- The markdown must match the HTML content (same facts, dates, prices).

Advertise mirrors in HTML:

```html
<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="/page.html.md" />
<link rel="describedby" href="/llms.txt" />
```

Or via HTTP header:

```http
Link: </page.html.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown", </llms.txt>; rel="describedby"
```

Do not create mirrors that are thin, outdated, or different in substance from
the HTML page — that is cloaking-adjacent and erodes trust.

## 4. Placement and serving

| Setup | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Static site | `public/llms.txt` → `/llms.txt` |
| Next.js App Router | `app/llms.txt/route.ts` (plain text) or `public/llms.txt` |
| WordPress | Root file via hosting; some SEO plugins add support |
| CDN | Serve from origin; do not rewrite to HTML |

Next.js route example:

```ts
// app/llms.txt/route.ts
export const dynamic = "force-static";

const body = `# Example Ltd

> UK ecommerce engineering studio building Shopify and Magento platforms.

## Services

- [Technical SEO](https://www.example.com/services/technical-seo.md): audits, fixes, and monitoring.
`;

export function GET() {
  return new Response(body, {
    headers: {
      "content-type": "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
      "cache-control": "public, max-age=3600",
    },
  });
}
```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://www.example.com/llms.txt
curl -s https://www.example.com/llms.txt
```

Expected: `200`, `text/plain`, starts with exactly one `# ` line.

## 5. Content selection

Include:

- Primary services/products with one-line descriptions.
- Best guides, docs, and references.
- Company/about/contact.
- Policies that matter to agents (pricing, licensing, returns).
- `## Optional` for secondary material.

Exclude:

- Duplicates and near-duplicates.
- Thin tag/archive/search pages.
- Pages behind login or geo-blocks.
- Anything you would not want quoted or cited.
- Keyword lists and internal notes.

## 6. Relationship to other files

| File | Purpose | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `robots.txt` | Crawler access policy | What may be fetched |
| `sitemap.xml` | Full URL inventory | What exists |
| `llms.txt` | Curated map for agents | What is worth reading |
| Markdown mirrors | Clean content for agents | How to read it |

They must not contradict each other. A URL in `llms.txt` should be crawlable,
canonical, and live.

## 7. Validation checklist

- [ ] `200`, `text/plain`, UTF-8.
- [ ] Exactly one H1.
- [ ] Blockquote summary after the H1 (recommended).
- [ ] Only H2 headings group lists.
- [ ] Every link is absolute, canonical, and returns 200.
- [ ] Markdown mirrors exist and match HTML.
- [ ] `## Optional` used for secondary links.
- [ ] File is current (reviewed date recorded).
- [ ] No claim that `llms.txt` guarantees citations or rankings.
- [ ] `robots.txt` does not block the file or the linked pages.
- [ ] Sitemap and `llms.txt` agree on canonical URLs.

## 8. Honest reporting

When reporting AI-search work:

- Say "published/updated `llms.txt` v2" — not "improved AI rankings".
- Measure referral traffic from AI surfaces and citation sampling separately.
- Record the date, prompt, and surface for any citation observation.
- Do not claim causation from a single change.
